diagnostic_evidence.quote:
The differential Helmholtz operator depends on the complex wavenumber with
non-negative real part and is formulated for general spatial dimension.

Consider a bounded
Lipschitz domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$ in $n\geq3$ dimensions

issues.failure_explanation: The unqualified general-dimensional summary overstates the n≥3 results. In dimension two at s=0, the displayed Laplace coefficients give DtN(0)1=0. Thus v=1 on a bounded annulus is harmonic and satisfies the transparent condition, but its gradient and wavenumber-indexed H¹ seminorm vanish while its L² and boundary H¹/² norms do not. The advertised unrestricted estimates therefore cannot cover this regime.

failure_location.quote:
We derive wavenumber independent trace and Friedrichs-type 
inequalities for the solution
space in wavenumber-indexed norms.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Explicitly restrict these advertised Friedrichs and trace contributions to n≥3, as the formal results already do.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract and contribution (b) materially overstate the dimensional scope of the small-wavenumber Friedrichs and trace guarantees.
issues.title: The advertised Friedrichs and trace scope includes an impossible two-dimensional regime
issues.why_classification: The supported correction excludes the entire advertised two-dimensional zero/small-wavenumber regime; the obstruction is an actual constant mode, not an omitted proof detail.

issues.failure_explanation: The defined H¹_loc space only controls compact subsets away from the boundary. For n=3, s=0 and x₀∈S_R, u(x)=|x−x₀|⁻¹ is harmonic and belongs to H¹_loc(B_R⁺), but its gradient is not square-integrable in any exterior collar containing x₀. Consequently the asserted H¹(ω,Δ) membership and H⁻¹/² normal trace do not follow.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require H¹ regularity in a collar up to S_R wherever these traces are invoked, rather than interior H¹_loc regularity alone.
issues.overall_effect: The blanket normal-trace assertion and subsequent trace shorthand for arbitrary exterior H¹_loc functions are invalid.
issues.title: Interior local H¹ regularity does not provide boundary traces
issues.why_classification: A standard local up-to-boundary regularity condition removes the counterexample without changing the wavenumber regimes or the spectral DtN estimates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\exists b\in\mathbb{R}\qquad u\left(  r\xi\right)  -b\log r\leq Cr^{-1}
\quad\text{as }r\rightarrow\infty\text{ uniformly in }\xi\in S_{1}.

issues.failure_explanation: Even for real-valued functions, the stated one-sided inequality does not prescribe a logarithmic asymptotic remainder. For every R>0, u(r)=−log(r/R) is a nonzero harmonic function with zero boundary data and satisfies SRCd with b=0 for sufficiently large r. Thus uniqueness fails also when R≠1. For complex-valued u, the displayed ordering is not defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the one-sided condition by |u(rξ)−b log r|≤Cr⁻¹, matching the logarithmic expansion used later.
issues.overall_effect: The logarithmic solution operator and its DtN comparison are not well-defined under the infinity condition actually written.
issues.title: The one-sided logarithmic infinity condition destroys uniqueness
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction of the infinity condition, supported by the later explicit expansion, and preserves the intended R≠1 result.

issues.failure_explanation: Independently of the missing modulus, b∈R is incompatible with the complex Sobolev data admitted by the paper. After correcting the remainder to a modulus bound, constant data g=i and R≠1 require b=i/log R, as the displayed solution formula shows. No real b can satisfy that condition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Allow b∈C in the logarithmic infinity condition.
issues.overall_effect: The logarithmic problem is not solvable for all data in its stated complex domain, and the asserted complex-linear logarithmic DtN operator is unavailable.
issues.title: A real logarithmic coefficient is incompatible with complex boundary data
issues.why_classification: Changing the coefficient field is a local correction directly supported by the explicit solution formula and preserves all intended complex-data guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: On the imaginary axis I_μ has two oscillatory contributions of the same size, not the asserted single exponential. For example, m=0 and ν=1/2 give f⁽²⁾(z)=sinh(z)/(πz), which vanishes at z=iπℓ for arbitrarily large ℓ; the asserted relative asymptotic cannot vanish there. The subsequent elimination of incoming coefficients therefore uses an invalid asymptotic in an advertised wavenumber regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Separate Re s>0 from purely imaginary s, retain both oscillatory terms on the latter, and use their differentiated leading terms to identify the non-radiating coefficient; equivalently use the Hankel basis already introduced in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: The radiation-based identification of the spectral solution and hence the DtN representation is not justified on the imaginary axis by this argument.
issues.title: The I-Bessel asymptotic used on the imaginary axis is false
issues.why_classification: A sector-correct local asymptotic calculation repairs this step without changing the solution construction or excluding imaginary wavenumbers.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Moreover, (\ref{fundsrad}) and the left relation for $f_{m,\nu
}^{\left(  1\right)  }$ in (\ref{fundsysasy}) reveal the implication

issues.failure_explanation: The cited asymptotics concern each fixed spherical-harmonic order. No summable bounds uniform in the order and direction are supplied. Consequently they cannot simply be passed through the infinite expansion to obtain the uniform-in-ξ bounds required by IC_strong for arbitrary H¹/² data. Correcting the individual Bessel asymptotics does not supply this missing argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the Green representation supplied in the appendix and establish uniform far-field estimates for its kernels and radial derivatives over the compact source sphere, or supply equivalent order-uniform summation estimates.
issues.overall_effect: Part 1b, identifying the Green-radiating solution with a strongly radiating solution for all admissible data, remains unproved.
issues.title: Modewise asymptotics do not establish uniform radiation of the infinite series
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial uniform far-field argument is required; the existing representation framework permits retaining the full result.

issues.failure_explanation: At purely imaginary interior Dirichlet eigenfrequencies, S has a nontrivial kernel despite uniqueness of the exterior radiating problem. For n=3 and s=iπ/R, sin(πr/R)/r is a nonzero regular interior solution with zero boundary value; its normal density produces such a kernel element. Equivalently, the constant-density single-layer trace is proportional to (1−e^(−2sR))/(2s), which vanishes at this s. The omitted interior nonresonance condition is essential to the claimed inversion.

failure_location.quote:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the unconditional inversion of S by the paper's spherical-harmonic construction, proving annular H¹ convergence using its coefficient bounds and constructing the radiating solution directly, including at interior resonances.
issues.overall_effect: The existence and continuity proof for the exterior solution operator fails at allowed imaginary wavenumbers.
issues.title: Exterior uniqueness does not imply invertibility of the single-layer operator
issues.why_classification: A nontrivial replacement of this existence step is necessary, but the spectral construction already present supports a contained repair without sacrificing any wavenumber regime.

issues.failure_explanation: For n=2 and m=0, F²=(d²−R²)/2>0, whereas the asserted bound is zero because m+2ν=0. The preceding table incorrectly assigns a logarithmic bound to this integral and also omits allowed half-integer cases such as n=3,m=0. Thus the displayed estimates do not prove the claimed H¹ continuity, even for constant boundary data.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the radial integrals and bound their sum by C(n,R,d)(1+m), treating the constant mode separately, then apply the stated Fourier characterization of H¹/².
issues.overall_effect: The appendix's quantitative proof of existence and continuity for the Laplace solution operator is invalid.
issues.title: The Laplace radial-norm estimates fail for allowed modes
issues.why_classification: Correct integration and a separate constant-mode estimate are routine local repairs preserving all existence and continuity claims.

issues.failure_explanation: The unit-sphere lower bound scales by 1/R. At s=0, a constant boundary function has DtN eigenvalue −(n−2)/R. In particular, n=3 and R=3 give −Re⟨DtN(0)g,g⟩=||g||²/3, contradicting the stated lower bound ||g||²/2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the lower coefficient by (n−2)/(2R) and scale this bound explicitly when passing from S₁ to S_R.
issues.overall_effect: Part (iii) is false for the unrestricted radii in the theorem, although the positivity needed later survives with the correct scaling.
issues.title: The DtN coercivity lower bound omits the radius scaling
issues.why_classification: This corrects a geometric constant without changing the wavenumber dependence, definiteness, or subsequent Friedrichs guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: Dominated convergence in the displayed pairing fixes g and h and establishes weak-operator continuity. It does not establish continuity in L(H¹/²,H⁻¹/²), which requires uniform control of |z_m(s)−z_m(s₀)|/(1+m) over all m. Pointwise coefficient continuity and the supplied O(1+m) bound do not make that supremum tend to zero.

follows from Lebesgue's dominated convergence theorem for the absolutely

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a locally uniform large-order estimate, for example z_{m,ν}(s)=−(m+2ν)+O_K(1/m) on compact wavenumber sets, and split the operator norm into finitely many modes and a uniformly small tail.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed bounded-operator continuity, including the operator-norm limit at zero, is not established by the proof.
issues.title: Dominated convergence does not establish operator-norm continuity
issues.why_classification: A new uniform-in-order estimate is needed, but it is a contained spectral lemma and can preserve the full continuity claim.

issues.failure_explanation: The exceptional additive constant cannot be absorbed into C|Im s| uniformly near zero. For n=2, constant g and s=−ik, the paper's K₀ expansion and Hankel identity give Im z_{0,0}(−ik) asymptotic to π/(2 log²k). Its ratio to k diverges as k→0, contradicting the displayed estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the c₂ contribution for the zero mode and bound it by the H¹/² part of the indexed boundary norm.
issues.overall_effect: The proof contains a false stronger L² imaginary-part bound, although the weaker indexed-norm bound in the theorem remains obtainable.
issues.title: The final imaginary-part estimate fails for the two-dimensional zero mode
issues.why_classification: The already proved exceptional-mode estimate supplies a direct local replacement preserving every stated part of the theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: The defined space only requires an H⁻¹/² normal trace, so its purported L²-flux norm need not be finite. Moreover, failure of the theorem's H⁻¹/² estimate would only yield a sequence with flux tending to zero in H⁻¹/², not in L². The stronger sequence assumed in the proof is therefore not justified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use H⁻¹/² consistently in the graph norm and the normalized contradiction sequence, and estimate boundary pairings by H⁻¹/²–H¹/² duality.
issues.overall_effect: The stated weak-flux Friedrichs inequality, and the corollary invoking it, are not proved by this contradiction setup.
issues.title: The Friedrichs proof replaces H⁻¹/² flux control by L² control
issues.why_classification: The required weaker norm works with the trace and DtN estimates already supplied; no extra regularity assumption or loss of scope is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
(The completeness of $H$ follows from the continuity of the
$\operatorname*{DtN}\left(  s\right)  $ operator by \Cref{thm:DtN}.)

Since this sequence is bounded in $H$, it admits a weakly convergent
subsequence with weak limit $u\in H$.

issues.failure_explanation: This is a union of kernels indexed by z, not generally a vector space. Two smooth functions can have the same nonzero Dirichlet trace and different normal traces DtN(z₁)g and DtN(z₂)g; their difference has zero Dirichlet trace but nonzero normal trace and belongs to none of the kernels. Continuity of the parameter family does not make this union Hilbert or ensure that a weak limit satisfies a condition for some finite z.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take compactness in the ambient H¹(Ω) space. Apply DtN coercivity and the trace estimate to each sequence member before taking the limit; the vanishing flux then forces the limiting constant's boundary trace to vanish.
issues.overall_effect: The weak-compactness step and the assertion that the limiting constant belongs to H are invalid.
issues.title: The union over wavenumbers is not a Hilbert space
issues.why_classification: A short sequence-level use of the already stated coercivity and trace bounds bypasses the fictitious Hilbert space and preserves the full uniform inequality.

issues.failure_explanation: The asserted formula covers n=2 and m=0, where its prefactor is 0/0. The constant eigenspace instead has multiplicity one, as the later Laplace calculation itself uses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State |J₀|=1 separately for n=2 and restrict the displayed quotient formula to the remaining cases.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit spectral multiplicity assertion is ill-defined at an allowed and subsequently used mode.
issues.title: The multiplicity formula is undefined for the two-dimensional constant mode
issues.why_classification: This is a local degenerate-case correction; the basis construction and all substantive spectral estimates remain unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: For n=2 and m≥1, ν=0 but the proof still uses the positive constant c₂. Letting ε tend to zero establishes only −Im z_{m,0}(s)≤c₂+Im s, not the theorem's sharp bound by Im s alone. The exceptional mode is (m,ν)=(0,0), rather than the whole dimension n=2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a mode-indexed barrier constant: c₂ only for (m,ν)=(0,0), and zero otherwise, then repeat the same maximum-principle step using the sharp boundary estimate already proved in Step 2.
issues.overall_effect: The maximum-principle argument as written establishes a weaker imaginary-part estimate for all positive modes in dimension two.
issues.title: The sharp imaginary bound is not established for nonzero modes in dimension two
issues.why_classification: The needed sharp boundary estimates are already present; correcting the case split preserves the theorem without a new lemma or any loss.
